gist: Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced a Your First Home scheme for first-time buyers.
The initiative offers 20 per cent equity loans for buyers with small deposits.
Conservatives warned the policy could increase buyer debt and drive up house prices.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has announced the Your First Home scheme to assist first-time buyers in England. The initiative offers a 20 per cent equity loan for new-build properties to buyers providing a 2.5 per cent deposit. Income, deposit, and property price caps will apply. Additionally, the government announced plans to make it easier for local councils to take over long-term empty homes and convert them into housing.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Supporters argue the policy helps young buyers lacking family financial support, while giving housebuilders confidence to build. However, Conservative critics warn that the scheme risks driving up property prices and increasing buyer debt burdens. Reports differ on announcement details: one outlet notes John Healey will formally announce the programme in the budget, while another attributes housing policy unveils to Angela Rayner.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Further details on how the equity loan scheme operates are expected in the upcoming Budget, with registration targeted to open by the end of 2026.

gist: The eviction of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal sparked nationwide protests across Spain over rising housing costs.
Protesters and politicians blamed investment funds and surging rents for deepening the housing crisis.
Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez promised swift measures while political parties remained deeply divided on housing.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: An 87-year-old disabled woman named Maricarmen Abascal was evicted from her Madrid home on a stretcher after being unable to afford a 230% rent hike demanded by an investment fund. The eviction sparked massive protests in Madrid and plazas across Spain, with thousands demanding a reckoning over housing costs.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The eviction became a symbol of Spain's broken housing market, where rents have outpaced average incomes. It reignited anger among citizens who view housing as their primary concern, highlighting political divisions and governance failures in protecting vulnerable tenants.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez promised to swiftly introduce new measures, while the junior government partner Sumar planned to push for a rent freeze and the expropriation of Maricarmen's former home. Meanwhile, protesters continue to demand bold actions from authorities.

fivew: Maricarmen Abascal, protesters, and Spanish politicians.

sections.text: Six writers share personal reflections on past behaviour they regret, including school pranks, difficult foster family dynamics, dating while hiding being gay, drunken insults at a hotel, ending a teenage relationship out of fear, and shouting at children over Lego.

sections.text: The essays highlight how personal insecurities, trauma, alcohol, and growing up can cause people to unintentionally hurt others.
